name: Total Cost Input for WooCommerce
author: ethereumicoio

sections.description:
Total Cost Input for WooCommerce plugin lets customers enter the amount of money they want to spend. The matching product quantity is calculated for them and shown right next to the sum (and, in the PRO version, the customer can also type the quantity and the two numbers stay in sync).

This plugin is ideal to sell products that can not be counted in portions, like liquids, powders, gas, cryptocurrencies, etc.

With this plugin used, your customer can just enter a sum, like $100 for example, and buy some amount of product you are selling, in grams, litres, bitcoins, etc.

It can be a valuable addition to your crypto selling store with the Cryptocurrency WordPress Plugin for WooCommerce!

FREE Features

  • Total Cost Input is a per-product product type: tick the checkbox on a product and that product, and only that product, asks for a sum instead of a quantity
  • The Total Cost Input field on the product page of an opted-in product: the customer enters the amount of money and the resulting quantity is calculated for them
  • A product-sale widget – the [total_cost_input_widget] shortcode and the Total Cost Input: Product Gutenberg block:
    • a dropdown of every product that can be bought right now (purchasable, in stock, visible in the catalog); the list shows product names only, without prices
    • an amount field in the site currency – the customer types the sum and the widget buys the matching quantity
    • a quantity field next to the sum: it is shown (read-only) and is updated as the customer types the amount, so the buyer sees the units before paying; the posted quantity is the same number
    • a Buy button that adds the product to the cart and takes the customer straight to the checkout
    • a configurable field order, so the card can be arranged the way you sell – including the product after the quantity – set per shortcode/block with the order attribute, in the block inspector, or site-wide on the settings screen
    • a 12-column grid: every field’s width is a span of 1 to 12 columns (or full for all twelve, which is the default), set per shortcode/block with the widths attribute, with the width selects in the block inspector, or as one line on the settings screen. A field that spans 12 columns takes the whole row, so a card of default fields stacks vertically and smaller spans sit in a row; fields whose spans add up to more than 12 wrap onto the next line – there is no separate layout switch
    • the Material design look by default: an elevated card, outlined fields and a filled button, so the widget looks finished without any styling
  • The Product Quantity Step setting – sell fractional quantities (enter 0.1 and the customer can buy 0.1, 0.2, 0.3 …), in the FREE version too

PRO Features

The PRO version includes all FREE features, plus:

  • Option to show both, the Total Cost Input and Quantity fields on the product page
  • The widget’s quantity field becomes editable – in place of the read-only quantity the customer can type the units too, and the two numbers are kept in sync in both directions: type a sum and the units follow, type the units and the sum follows
  • The widget’s product list restriction – sell only the products you choose, not the whole catalog
  • The widget’s custom button text instead of Buy
  • The widget’s theme style – apply the style of the site theme to the widget, so it inherits the theme’s background, borders, font and corner radii and the plugin only keeps the layout
  • The widget’s custom style, set in the block inspector or on the settings screen – background colour of the widget and of the button, text colour, font family, font size and the corner radius of the widget and of the button, on top of the included Material default
  • The widget’s vendor restriction – on a WC Vendors, Dokan or WCFM page the dropdown offers that vendor’s products only

Not supported yet

Block-based product surfaces are not supported yet. The Total Cost Input field works on the classic single-product template and on the classic cart and checkout. The block versions of those pages (the Single Product block, the Cart and Checkout blocks) render the quantity field on the client side and therefore ignore the plugin’s field:

  • Single Product block – no Total Cost Input field;
  • Cart and Checkout blocks – no money/quantity synchronisation.

Use the classic templates (or the [total_cost_input_widget] shortcode / block, which is unaffected) until a future release adds the block support.

sections.installation:
• Install and activate it as you would any other plugin.
  • Make a new WooCommerce product, or just check the Total Cost Input checkbox on an existing one.
  • To sell from a widget, drop the [total_cost_input_widget] shortcode (or the Total Cost Input: Product block) into a page.
sections.changelog:
2.0.0

  • Rewritten on a layered architecture: app/ is split into Domain / Views / Controllers / Modules, and Infrastructure\Hooks is the only place that registers a hook. The plugin option, the product meta key, the public hooks and the total_cost asset handle are unchanged, so an upgrade keeps the configuration.
  • The Total Cost Input per-product checkbox is now part of the FREE version.
  • The Product Quantity Step setting is FREE too: enter 0.1 and the customer can buy 0.1, 0.2, 0.3 … without a licence.
  • The global/quantity-input.php template override was rebased on WooCommerce 10.1.0 (unified woocommerce_before/after_quantity_input_field hooks, aria-label, conditional size / max).
  • The PRO-only “show the quantity field too” option no longer hides the field with CSS: the standard quantity input is a hidden field and the visible one is rendered by PRO only.
  • New product-sale widget: the [total_cost_input_widget] shortcode and the Total Cost Input: Product Gutenberg block – a dropdown of every product that can be bought right now (names only, no prices) and a Buy button that adds the product to the cart and takes the customer straight to the checkout.
  • PRO: the widget’s amount field (a sum in the site currency), the product-list restriction, a custom button text, a theme style (the widget inherits the site theme’s own styling), a custom style (widget and button background, text colour, font family and size, corner radius) and the vendor restriction on WC Vendors / Dokan / WCFM pages.
  • The widget is a flat 12-column grid: every field claims a span of 1 to 12 columns and a field that spans all twelve takes the whole row, so the card stacks by default and smaller spans make a row. The old layout attribute/option (vertical/horizontal) is gone – the spans are the layout.
  • The front end is a Vite + React bundle. jQuery is no longer used – not a dependency, not in the code – and assets/widget.js and the root *.js / *.min.js files are gone.
  • A widget that renders nothing publishes the reason (empty_catalog, no_vendor, no_vendor_products) through total_cost_input_for_woocommerce_widget_empty.
  • The products attribute of the widget is cast with (int), so a negative id means “no products” rather than product 1.
  • Requires WordPress 6.6 and PHP 7.4; tested up to WordPress 7.1 and WooCommerce 11.2.
  • Known limitation: block-based product surfaces (the Single Product block, the Cart and Checkout blocks) are not supported yet.

1.1.3

  • freemius library version update
  • tested up to WordPress 7.1 and WooCommerce 11.2

1.1.2

  • freemius library version update

1.1.1

  • freemius library version update

1.1.0

  • The Product Quantity Step setting is introduced. Enter 0.1 to allow customer to buy 0.1, 0.2, 0.3, e.t.c. quantity of your products.

1.0.2

  • WooCommerce global/quantity-input.php template update to the latest version

1.0.1

  • freemius library version update

1.0.0

  • Initial release.

the product screen: the per-product Total Cost Input checkbox on the General tab of the product data panel
the settings screen: Product Quantity Step, Widget field order, Widget widths (a 12-column span per field: 1 … 12 or full) and the Widget style row
the same product card the other way round: a typed quantity moves the total (0.05 units at 100 are 5.00), so the two fields stay in sync in both directions

the sale widget in a page (FREE): the product dropdown, the amount field and the Quantity shown next to it as a disabled display that follows the amount (9.9 buys 0.099), in the default Material card, with the page text around it
the same Free widget with the product list open: the custom list shows the product names only (BTC, ETH), with no prices, and it is not clipped by the card
the same Free widget on one row: the amount, the disabled Quantity (0.099 at 9.9), the product dropdown and Buy share the row through their 12-column spans
the same widget in PRO with the Material style: the amount field and the editable quantity field next to it (9.9 buys 0.099)
the same Professional widget with the product list open: names only, no prices, not clipped

the Total Cost Input block in the block editor with its inspector open: the Field order rows, the four Width selects (Product, You pay, Quantity, Buy button) and the opened Style panel with its mode, colours, font, font size and corner radii
the Professional widget with a custom style: its own card and button colours, font, font size and corner radii, stacked
the same custom style on one row: the amount, the quantity, the product dropdown and the button sharing the row, painted by the block's colours, font and radii, with the 4/3/2/3 12-column spans
the 12-column grid in action: You pay spans 4 of 12 columns, the quantity 4, the product dropdown 1 and the Buy button 3 - 4/4/1/3 adds up to the full row, so all four fields sit on one line
